behaviours.summary: Registers the application's one configurator, which hands each command sent on the CommandBus to the Decider that can handle it, loads that aggregate's event stream and appends the event it returns.
Routes every command implementing the bounded context's command interface to its aggregate type, taking the stream id from the command and from each event.
Writes every event variant of the aggregate with an @type discriminator, so the stream's events round-trip through JSON.
The Decider answers the command with the slice's event, carrying the command's id and payload.
The Decider returns no event when the stream already holds the slice's event, so a repeated command appends nothing.
The Decider enforces no invariant and rejects no command; the slice's rules are left to the developer.
The command and the event carry one placeholder String; the real payload fields, and copying them into the event, are left to the developer.
A POST to the slice's path takes the command as its body, sends it on the CommandBus and answers 202 Accepted.

behaviours.summary: On the projected event the projection inserts the row keyed by the aggregate id, or updates the existing one, with the event's order as the row's version.
An event whose order is not newer than the row's version is skipped, so a redelivered event changes nothing.
A subscription reset deletes every row, so the replay that follows rebuilds the read model from the events.
A GET on the view's path returns every row of the read model.

behaviours.summary: On the triggering event the processor loads or creates the process's TodoList keyed by the aggregate id, marks it started and saves it.
A redelivered event finds its TodoList already started and returns before dispatching or saving again.
The send of the next command is commented out, so the TodoList is marked dispatched but nothing is sent; the command to dispatch is left to the developer.
No handler exists for the events that advance or complete the process, and the TodoList is never marked completed; they are left to the developer.
Attempts are never counted and no compensating command is issued on terminal failure; bounded retries and compensation are left to the developer.
